standard_prerequisites: The stalk of a quasi-coherent module at a geometric point of an algebraic space, expressed as a base change of the stalk on an etale chart
The identification of the local ring at a geometric point with the strict henselization of the local ring of a chart, and the flatness of the chart map on local rings
Flat base change of lengths of modules over local rings, and the identification of the quotient by the maximal ideal with the residue field
core_obligations: Take an etale chart and a point of it mapping to the given point, and recall that the local ring at the geometric point is the strict henselization of the local ring of the chart at that point
Express the stalk at the geometric point as the base change of the stalk on the chart along that map of local rings

Conclude that the two lengths agree, using flat base change of lengths and the fact that the quotient of the strict henselization by the ideal generated by the maximal ideal of the chart is its residue field
proof_roadmap: Identify the geometric point local ring with a strict henselization and rewrite the stalk as a base change
Apply flat base change of lengths and the residue field identification
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the etale local nature of the length of a quasi-coherent module at a point at source lines 471-487, label lemma-length, whose proof occupies source lines 489-508. The proof is short but has a precise structure: it replaces the local ring at the geometric point by the strict henselization of the local ring of an etale chart, rewrites the stalk as the base change of the stalk on the chart along that map of local rings, and then applies flat base change of lengths together with the identification of the quotient of the strict henselization by the ideal generated by the maximal ideal of the chart with its residue field. The counted statement records neither the strict henselization nor the base change formula.
